The analysis shows that **50** crime incidents are linked by a single modus operandi, identified as **MO001**. This MO is described as “**Breaking through rear windows at night**” and carries the signature “**leaves door unlocked**,” indicating a consistent pattern of entry across the cases.

All of the paired crimes revolve around a central **BURGLARY** (ID 14303245) that shares this method with a wide spectrum of offenses. The other offenses include **OTHER OFFENSE**, **WEAPONS VIOLATION**, **BATTERY**, **NARCOTICS**, **THEFT**, **PUBLIC PEACE VIOLATION**, **DECEPTIVE PRACTICE**, **CRIMINAL TRESPASS**, **ASSAULT**, **CRIMINAL DAMAGE**, and even another **THEFT** (ID 14303665) linked directly to the same burglary. This breadth of crime types suggests that the same perpetrators or a coordinated group are applying the same entry technique to very different illegal activities.

Because the same entry method appears across such diverse categories, investigators can focus on the common “rear‑window break‑in” signature to trace potential links between suspects, locations, or organized crews. Understanding that **MO001** is the unifying factor may help prioritize surveillance of properties vulnerable to night‑time rear‑window breaches.

Would you like to see which individuals or organizations are most frequently connected to these **MO001** incidents?

cypher.name: Crimes sharing the same Modus Operandi
cypher.cypher: MATCH (c1:Crime)-[:MATCHES_MO]->(m:ModusOperandi)<-[:MATCHES_MO]-(c2:Crime) WHERE c1.id < c2.id RETURN c1.id AS crime1_id, c1.type AS crime1_type, c2.id AS crime2_id, c2.type AS crime2_type, m.id AS mo_id, m.description AS mo_description, m.signature_element AS mo_signature LIMIT 50
